card.band: 8h. Many operations with filter and colour-space details; frontier covers the simple majority, tolerance-level filters decide the rest. Weaker models stop at format IO.
card.cheat: Wrapping an installed oiiotool or Python imaging lib; closed by an image with no such binaries and no network.
card.grading: Hidden command lines on generated images, run against the real oiiotool outside the image; outputs compared by pixel tolerance per operation, exact for integer ops. Credit per operation bucket.
card.reference: OpenImageIO itself as oracle; our reference implementation size is not measured and would be several thousand lines.
card.task: /app ships the oiiotool command documentation for a subset (resize, crop, over, colour convert, channel ops, stats, diff) and test images. Agent builds a CLI in Rust or Go that reads and writes PNG/TIFF/EXR subsets and implements these operations.
card.title: oiiotool image-operation subset matched to OpenImageIO

source_notes: Library for reading, processing and writing images

facts.claim: OpenImageIO repo has release tag v3.2.1.2
Release v3.2.1.2 has no code changes (tag made to force a Python 3.15 wheel build); no oiiotool or OCIO changes listed. Release page says 15 Oct, commit message says Oct 14, 2026
Licence is Apache License 2.0 with no extra bundled-component terms in LICENSE
oiiotool.rst documentation exists at v3.2.1.2 under src/doc
Debian/Ubuntu package openimageio-tools ships the oiiotool binary (older versions 2.5.18.0 and 3.1.18.x seen; not 3.2.1.2)
oiiotool --colorconvert works without an external OCIO config (built-in fallback)
A complete Go or Rust reimplementation of the oiiotool CLI exists
Rust crates image and exrs provide PNG/TIFF/EXR codecs and imageops, but no oiiotool CLI port

full_card.band: Full seed scope is about 20h for a frontier agent; trimmed scope (PNG+TIFF+EXR ZIP/none, listed ops, sRGB-linear only) is about 8-20h. Frontier likely lands 0.3-0.6 of reference; a 0.9 pass needs the trimmed scope and parallel subagents
full_card.build_cost: Writing our reference: several thousand lines, about 3-5 days; oracle build is apt install (fast) or source build (30-60 min on 8 cores); smoke_build was empty, so no offline build evidence
full_card.deliverable: Rust or Go CLI accepting oiiotool-style command lines for PNG/TIFF/EXR subset reads and writes plus resize, crop, over, colorconvert (sRGB/linear only), channel ops, stats, diff
full_card.gates_anticheat: Image has no oiiotool, no Python PIL/OpenEXR/OIIO bindings, no network; grader rejects binaries wrapping system tools; build config and tests are read-only
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden command lines over generated images, compared per operation bucket by pixel tolerance (exact for integer ops); generator gives thousands of cases
full_card.local_fit: CPU only, a few GB at most for test images; no GPU; fits 8 cores 16 GB; EXR and TIFF codecs must be written in-house with stdlib zlib
full_card.lookup: partial: Rust image and exrs crates exist but are not an oiiotool CLI; no Go or Rust port found; OIIO itself is famous and recallable only in outline
full_card.provenance: OpenImageIO v3.2.1.2 tag, Apache-2.0, C++, 2387 stars, not a fork, not archived; git head ed2af36
full_card.reference: OpenImageIO itself as oracle (Apache-2.0); our own reference for the trimmed subset must be written, several thousand lines
full_card.ships: Oracle and reference live outside the image: grader runs real oiiotool (apt openimageio-tools or a built v3.2.1.2) on generated images; /app ships oiiotool docs for the subset, test images, and an OCIO config file if colorconvert needs one

spike_plan.kill_if: Outputs differ across repeat runs, or colorconvert needs a config that cannot be shipped under its licence, or resize cannot be matched within tolerance by any reasonable kernel.
spike_plan.pass_if: Deterministic outputs on repeat runs; at least 4 op buckets reproducible at tolerance; colorconvert works with a shipped config or sRGB/linear alone; EXR none/zip written by oiiotool is readable by a minimal reader.
steps: In a networked throwaway container, apt install openimageio-tools (or build v3.2.1.2 from source if the apt version differs; record the version used).
Run oiiotool --version and --colorconfiginfo; check whether --colorconvert sRGB to linear works with no OCIO config set. If it needs a config, note which config file must ship.
Generate about 30 command lines covering PNG and TIFF read/write, resize, crop, over, colorconvert, channel ops, stats, diff; run each twice and compare outputs byte-for-byte for determinism.
Compare resize output on an 8-bit PNG against a quick reference (e.g. a naive Lanczos) to see how far a from-scratch filter is from OIIO's kernel; note the tolerance needed.
Check the EXR subset: write with oiiotool --compression none and zip, and confirm the header parses with a minimal reader.
Confirm the planned image has no oiiotool, no PIL, no OpenEXR bindings.

v1.summary: The repository, tag v3.2.1.2 and Apache-2.0 licence check out, and a packaged oiiotool exists as an offline oracle outside the image. The seed as written (PNG/TIFF/EXR plus full colour conversion) is about 22 frontier hours, so it passes only if trimmed to the PNG/TIFF/EXR-ZIP subset with sRGB/linear colour work on the 20-hour tier.

v2.note: Survives. The tag, the Apache-2.0 licence and the absence of any existing oiiotool port are confirmed, and real oiiotool running outside the image gives an unlimited differential oracle with per-op buckets. The 22h estimate against a 20h tier is probably too high: in calibration, comparable ports finished in 23-104 min. So retier to 8h and keep the trimmed scope (PNG, TIFF, EXR none/zip, listed ops, sRGB/linear only), or the task risks K8. Open gaps: (1) the oiiotool.rst link is dead, so find the real doc path at the tag. (2) The apt build is 3.1.18 while the source is 3.2.1.2: pin one oracle and ship its docs. (3) The colorconvert fallback without an OCIO config is unconfirmed. (4) Rust's standard library has no inflate and Go ships image/png, so fix the language and the vendored crates, or the buckets get uneven. (5) Matching resize filter kernels and EXR half rounding needs per-op tolerances that a different valid implementation can pass. (6) The reference is unwritten, several thousand lines, 3-5 days.
